title: Cal AI's growth bottleneck: fixing the "it's not accurate" narrative
summary: Zach reflects after Cal AI's best month (over $3M in May), explaining that the biggest growth bottleneck is public skepticism about accuracy. He lays out how he plans to counter it with influencer scripts, honest messaging and educating users on features beyond the viral scan, and what he would do differently on future projects.

principles.text: Find your biggest growth bottleneck by reading what people actually say about you, then make fixing it the main priority.
principles.quote: I'm analyzing all of our social media posts that have went out recently, and I'm realizing that I think the biggest bottleneck for our growth is really the fact that so many people still don't think Cali is accurate.

principles.text: Address trust and credibility objections from the start of scaling, before critics define the narrative.
principles.quote: I think from earlier on we should have handled this issue because now it's like kind of out of hand and it's going to be a big uphill battle.

principles.text: Viral content often shows only one feature; educate users on the rest of the product.
principles.quote: all of our marketing material really just shows the scanning feature because that's what goes viral. But so so most people don't know we have the database and barcode. So that's what we're trying to start educating users on.

principles.text: Be honest about product limits in messaging to build credibility against skepticism.
principles.quote: Cali does not have X-ray vision. can only track what it sees. It won't know how much oil you're using, so it will estimate the typical portion. And the scanner is not always 100% accurate. It's closer to 90%.

principles.text: Test a short message first, assess how people take it, then double down with longer content.
principles.quote: I think I'm going to start with this. assess how people take it and then double down.

principles.text: Sometimes you must take a step back to move two steps forward; chip away at a brick wall until you break through.
principles.quote: it kind of feels like we're taking a step back right now to do this, but it's in order to take two steps forward, which is sometimes necessary is what I've learned.
